title: Postman exports: credential-shaped values stored in an unselected auth type or a disabled variable
summary: Two situations a Postman export can express in its own bytes. A collection auth object whose type selects one scheme while another scheme's attribute array, holding a credential-shaped value, is still stored. A variable or environment entry marked disabled (or enabled false) that still holds a credential-shaped value. No fixture is authored.
rationale: The SDK documents that a request can hold the data of several auth types with one selected, and that disabled variables are skipped by lookup. Whether a value that Postman will not use is still to be treated as a credential is a judgement the sources do not settle: the bytes are as present as in the active case and could be a leftover real value, but nothing documented says that inactive storage changes or keeps its confidentiality. The case records the ambiguity instead of choosing, so that neither a must-flag nor a must-not-flag label is invented.

expectation.rationale: Candidate outcomes: must-flag (the value is a credential-shaped literal in a credential-bearing field; being unselected or disabled is a runtime state of the application, not a property of the bytes), or may-flag (an inactive value may be a leftover, so a report is allowed but not required). The sources show only how Postman treats such values (an unselected auth type keeps its attribute data; a disabled variable is ignored by lookup; a disabled header is not sent), and not how confidentiality follows. A maintainer decision with a named non-author reviewer would settle it; an agent cannot. Until then no fixture is authored and the case is not counted as a true or false negative.

sources.supports: A request auth definition can hold the attribute data of several auth types at once (for example basic and digest) while one type is selected with use().
Disabled variables are not returned by has() or get(); a disabled variable is not updated by set(), which adds a new variable instead.
A variable and a header can carry a disabled boolean, and a disabled header is not sent with requests.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04; no scanner was run. Needs human: outcome decision (maintainer, with a non-author reviewer); an agent run does not write project-policy.
